title: Transmissions, Clutches and Final Drives
author: Erudior
description: Trace manual, conventional automatic, automated manual, dual-clutch, pulley CVT and power-split drives. Compare final drives and axle joints, then assemble and measure a gear trainer. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added an individual parts atlas, hands-on modification workshop, instance-level build ledger and pre/post verification.

lessons.title: Follow a selected ratio
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Engine and Drivetrain Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

A manual gearbox selects gear pairs using clutches or synchronizers. An automatic can hold or couple elements of a planetary set with clutches and brakes. Its torque converter transmits torque through fluid and may lock mechanically. A CVT can vary its effective ratio continuously. Identify the architecture before choosing a fluid check, shift diagnosis or test specification.

## Worked shop case

On a simple gear pair the 15-tooth input turns a 45-tooth output. The input makes three revolutions for one output revolution. Two external gears also reverse rotation direction.

## Guided practice

A 12-tooth input drives a 48-tooth output. How many input turns produce one output turn?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A working hand-driven transmission trainer and its verified ratio sheet.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Manual clutch or torque converter at launch
topics: Manual clutch or torque converter at launch
lessons.body:
In a typical constant-mesh manual, torque travels from flywheel to friction disc, gearbox input, selected gears and final drive. The pressure plate clamps the disc. A cable or hydraulic release system lifts that load when the driver presses the pedal. Synchronizer friction matches speeds before engagement teeth lock the chosen gear to its shaft. The clutch creates heat while slipping during launch. Fully engaged at steady speed, it should transmit torque without sustained slip.

A conventional automatic starts through a torque converter. The pump impeller drives fluid into the turbine; the stator redirects returning flow and can multiply torque when the turbine is slow. A commanded lockup clutch can couple the two sides mechanically. Internal clutches and brakes select gear ratios. Both architectures can deliver the same wheel torque at a given overall reduction once mechanically coupled. They need different controls, thermal capacity, pedal space, mounts, flywheel or flexplate, and service access.

## Worked shop case

In a manual, engine rpm rises at steady road speed in a fully engaged fixed gear on a verified non-slipping tire. Investigate the clutch and its release system. For the same observation in an automatic first obtain selected gear, input and output speed, lockup command and actual slip. An intentional converter unlock or downshift can produce the observation during normal operation.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A donor automatic is sold without controller or cooler. What changes in the manual-versus-automatic budget?
step: Price the compatible controller, harness, selector and cooling circuit.
step: For the manual price pedal clearance, compatible clutch actuation and flywheel.
answer: Evaluate complete installed systems and service space before comparing purchase prices.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Trace both paths on two identified donor diagrams. Annotate launch, engaged cruise, power interruption, heat rejection and compatible controls. Record the actual service access or connector position on one isolated unit.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Planetary gearsets, valve bodies and shift diagnosis
topics: Planetary gearsets, valve bodies and shift diagnosis
lessons.body:
The sun gear meshes with planets on a carrier. The planets mesh with an internally toothed ring. Power flow depends on which member is driven, held or used as output. In a simple set with ring fixed, sun input and carrier output, input turns per output turn equal 1 + ring teeth / sun teeth. Locking any two members together makes the set rotate as one. Production transmissions combine sets, clutches, brakes and sometimes one-way elements. The same transmission may use different elements in reverse and forward ranges.

The pump supplies hydraulic flow; the valve body routes it. The controller uses sensors and solenoids to command circuits and clutch apply timing. A delayed engagement can arise from low supply pressure, a leaking circuit or a command problem. A speed change by itself cannot distinguish them. Use the exact transmission identification, element-application chart, fluid type, temperature window and authorized measurement procedure.

## Worked shop case

A training set has a 30-tooth sun and 60-tooth ring. With the ring held the carrier turns once per three sun turns. If a clutch locks sun and ring together, it takes one input turn. On a real unit a ratio error in one range suggests checking which apply elements are unique to that range before pricing a rebuild.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: An identified simple set has a fixed 72-tooth ring and a 24-tooth sun input. What should a marked carrier do?
step: Calculate one plus 72 divided by 24.
step: Note that the fixed member is essential to the calculation.
answer: Four input turns produce one carrier turn in the same direction.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Label the three members of a hand-driven model. Mark positions, predict rotation, then count at least two carrier turns. Attach a donor application chart and identify one diagnostic test for a failed shift.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Single-clutch automated manuals and dual-clutch gearboxes
topics: Single-clutch automated manuals and dual-clutch gearboxes
lessons.body:
An automated manual can use one conventional friction clutch and actuators to operate clutch and selector. Engine torque normally drops as that unit unloads one gear and selects the next. A dual-clutch transmission typically routes alternating ratios through two clutches and two input paths. The controller can preselect the next ratio on the unloaded path, then hand torque across by coordinating the clutches. An unexpected shift can still require another selection. Paddle shifters identify a driver control and reveal little about the internal design.

Wet clutches use oil to carry heat away; fluid specification, pump and cooler capacity matter. Dry clutches shed heat through their surrounding structure; extended creeping or holding on a grade through clutch slip increases temperature. Verify the actual launch device, actuator type, control integration and adaptation procedure. A wet or dry clutch describes the friction pack; separate gear lubricant requirements can still apply.

## Worked shop case

A kit must creep for long periods and accommodate a specific donor controller. Candidate A is a dry DCT with no approved duty data; B is a wet DCT with compatible cooling and documented duty capacity. B supplies evidence for that requirement if the cooler fits and measurements confirm capacity. Pedal count alone would miss the thermal issue.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: Why can an automated manual pause even when the accelerator position stays constant?
step: Trace torque through its single input clutch.
step: Identify when the selector unloads and re-engages a ratio.
answer: Clutch actuation and the gear change can interrupt torque; compare commanded versus measured behavior.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Draw torque flow in first and second for one identified DCT. Compare the service fluids, control adaptations and thermal provisions against a single-clutch automated manual.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Belt and chain CVTs versus power-split hybrid drives
topics: Belt and chain CVTs versus power-split hybrid drives
lessons.body:
A pulley CVT changes its effective running diameters as a metal belt or chain moves along opposed pulley faces. Clamping force must transmit torque without uncontrolled slip. Controls regulate ratio and pressure, so correct fluid and temperature matter. Launch devices vary by model. Engine speed can remain near a target as road speed rises smoothly. Compare commanded to measured input/output ratio under the documented conditions.

Some hybrids sold as eCVTs use planetary power-split devices and motor-generators. Their continuously variable engine-to-wheel speed relationship comes from electrical-machine speed control and gear constraints. Those examples contain no belt-and-pulley variator. Other hybrid designs use different couplings; verify a power-flow schematic for the exact generation. Component lists, diagnostic data, training and electrical isolation requirements follow the actual design.

## Worked shop case

Two customers describe constant engine speed during acceleration. One vehicle has a metal-chain variator, the other a planetary power split. A technician can compare shaft-speed ratio to pulley commands on the first. On the second, interpret engine speed, machine speeds, state of charge and requested torque together using the hybrid service information.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A diagram shows variable-diameter pulleys and a chain. What should the next service lookup address?
step: Identify the transmission code and launch device.
step: Check its specified fluid, fill procedure and ratio/pressure data.
answer: Use the pulley CVT procedure applicable to that code.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Put a pulley CVT and a documented power-split transaxle side by side on paper. Label energy paths, diagnostic parameters and components available for external inspection. Keep high-voltage work within the qualified service plan.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Transaxles, transfer cases, differentials and axle joints
topics: Transaxles, transfer cases, differentials and axle joints
lessons.body:
A transaxle combines transmission and final drive in one assembly. A longitudinal rear-drive layout commonly sends torque through a propeller shaft to a separate differential. Front-drive half shafts often use an inboard plunging joint for length change and an outboard constant-velocity joint for steering angle. A single Cardan joint operating at an angle creates cyclic output-speed variation. A paired driveshaft depends on correct phasing and operating angles. Compare joint angle, plunge, travel, flange compatibility, critical speed and rated torque using the chosen hardware's engineering data.

An open axle differential permits unequal wheel speeds through a turn and delivers approximately equal axle-shaft torques, ignoring friction. A clutch or helical limited-slip unit can bias torque subject to its design, load and available traction. A locked axle constrains both wheel speeds. An AWD system may allow front/rear speed difference through a center differential or controlled coupling. Many part-time 4WD systems mechanically couple the axles when engaged. Tire size and permissible surfaces matter; a coupled driveline can wind up on a high-grip turn.

## Worked shop case

With both tires loaded, one wheel can support only 100 N·m before slipping. An ideal open differential delivers about 100 N·m to the other shaft too. A 3:1 torque-bias specification may permit up to about 300 N·m on the high-traction side in the specified conditions. It does not promise that amount with one wheel fully unloaded or with insufficient engine torque.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A fixed gearbox ratio of 3 and final drive of 4 receive 100 N·m. Predict torque entering the differential after reduction, ignoring loss.
step: Multiply the two ratios.
step: Multiply 100 by the combined 12:1.
answer: 1,200 N·m is total final-drive output torque before distribution to the wheels.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Select one actual axle and one alternative. Map gearbox location, driven wheels, joint types, center coupling, serviceable bearings and shaft length at ride height and travel extremes. Record the measurement method and the source of each allowable range.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Choose a serviceable drive ratio
lessons.body:
Select a target output speed first. Write down each ratio as input turns per output turn and define the load assumptions. An open differential allows left and right wheel speeds to differ in a turn. A final drive and axle pair must suit torque, travel and joint angles. Using a gearbox's ratio alone misses the final reduction.

## Worked shop case

At a fixed 1,800 rpm input, a 2:1 gearbox and 3:1 final drive give 300 rpm at the differential carrier. Straight-ahead equal wheel speed is assumed.

## Guided practice

At 2,400 input rpm with 2:1 and 4:1 reductions, what carrier rpm do you predict?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Select gear pairs for two reductions on your trainer. Draw shafts, supports, guards and the indicator location. Predict turns and direction for each pair. Give the acceptance check and explain which automatic or manual service tasks need vehicle-specific data.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Set up a hand-driven gear pair
lessons.body:
Identify bearings, thrust surfaces, shaft support and mesh. On an isolated trainer, lock one gear according to its instructions and gently rock the other without rolling through the mesh. An indicator near the specified radius records backlash. A powered assembly needs its own procedure. A teaching gear train must not be used to set a road differential's preload or contact pattern.

## Worked shop case

A pointer moves 0.08 mm one way and 0.05 mm the other from zero. Total backlash at the stated radius is 0.13 mm. Moving the pointer to a different radius would change the reading.

## Guided practice

An indicator moves between 0.02 and 0.17 mm during the specified lash check. Give the range in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

Before handling transmissions, secure the load on rated equipment and address hydraulic accumulators, rotating parts and stored spring energy. A covered workplace determines applicable guarding and energy-control procedures. Apply brake/clutch asbestos controls to suspect clutch dust. Used transmission oil goes into the appropriate identified recovery stream. Record isolation, supported load and waste disposition.

[OSHA — control of hazardous energy, 29 CFR 1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147) · [OSHA — machine guarding, 29 CFR 1910.212](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212) · [OSHA — brake/clutch asbestos controls, 29 CFR 1910.1001 Appendix F](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1001AppF) · [EPA — used oil requirements for businesses, 40 CFR Part 279](https://www.epa.gov/hw/managing-used-oil-answers-frequent-questions-businesses)

## Workshop preparation

Use a hand-driven guarded trainer only. Isolate it before adjustment. Keep fingers and loose clothing away from mesh and never energize an open gearbox.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Predict the gearing change before ordering a differential
topics: Predict the gearing change before ordering a differential
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Clutch, gearbox and final drive, Driver controls and transmission details, Transmission subcomponents and seals. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Clutch and flywheel change
- Shorter shifter throw
- Final-drive ratio change
- Limited-slip differential
- Manual transmission conversion
- Transmission cooler for sustained load

## Worked example

With a 1.00 top gear, 4.10 final drive and 2.00 m rolling circumference, 100 km/h means roughly 833 wheel rpm and 3,417 engine rpm in a coupled, lossless speed model. A 3.50 final gives about 2,917 rpm. At identical engine torque the 4.10 gives about 17% more wheel torque than the 3.50.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: If both ratios are tested at the same road speed, is equal engine torque guaranteed?
step: Use the calculated engine speeds to locate each point on the torque curve.
answer: No. Recalculate wheel torque using actual engine torque at each operating point.
```

## Independent workshop

Build a hand-driven shifter or ratio fixture. Record input/output travel or turns, trace detents/retention and compare two setups before selecting donor parts.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Separate a ratio error from slip
lessons.body:
When input and output speeds do not match prediction, check selected gear, clutch or converter state and the test condition. A wheel that turns freely on an open differential can invalidate a one-wheel ratio inference. On an automatic, distinguish a controller's command from evidence that a clutch actually applied. Use model-specific scan and pressure procedures.

## Worked shop case

A hand-driven trainer with positively engaged gears repeatedly yields one output turn for four input turns when the drawing predicts three. Count the actual teeth and inspect which pair is engaged before blaming slip.

## Guided practice

A verified 4:1 trainer produces three full output turns. How many input turns are expected?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

Both tooth-count and shaft-mark methods support the reported ratio, with repeatable lash readings. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Launch element; Flywheel, flexplate and release; Ratio selection; Shift actuation; Continuously variable drive; Gearbox position and driven axles; Axle differential; Half shafts and propeller shafts. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Launch element | Single-plate friction clutch / torque converter with lockup | Clutch capacity and converter lockup behavior imply different heat, controls and service. | Compare input and engine speeds under an identified operating condition. |
| Flywheel, flexplate and release | Single-mass / dual-mass flywheel / flexplate; cable / hydraulic release | Crank interface, starter ring, alignment, inertia and release travel are package-specific. | Document the matched flywheel or flexplate, pilot, fasteners and available release travel from source data. |
| Ratio selection | Synchronized manual / planetary automatic | Manual dog engagement and automatic apply elements create different failure signatures. | Trace power in two gears and identify a shared and a unique element. |
| Shift actuation | Driver-operated / single-clutch automated / wet or dry DCT | Shifting can interrupt one torque path or hand it to a preselected path. | Review actuator commands, thermal duty and adaptations for the actual unit. |
| Continuously variable drive | Belt or chain variator / planetary power-split eCVT | Pulleys vary effective diameter; a power-split device coordinates gear and electrical-machine speeds. | Identify physical parts on diagrams and name the diagnostic data unique to each. |
| Gearbox position and driven axles | FWD transaxle / RWD longitudinal / AWD / part-time 4WD | A coupled transfer case may constrain front and rear speeds; packaging changes shaft lengths. | Map the output paths and the permitted operating surfaces and tire tolerances. |
| Axle differential | Open / helical or clutch limited-slip / locking | Differentiate torque bias from a constraint on wheel speeds. | Record installed final ratio, required lubricant and specified operating checks. |
| Half shafts and propeller shafts | Plunging or fixed CV joint / Cardan pair | Axle travel needs plunge and angular capacity; Cardan layouts depend on phasing and angle. | Document plunge, joint angle range and shaft clearance for a reviewer. |

references.body:

Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Clutch disc

**Function.** Transmits torque by friction between flywheel and cover.

**Design.** Choose spline, diameter, friction material and torque/duty capacity.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Center the matched disc in the prescribed direction before fitting cover.

**Verify.** Check release, engagement and slip under documented conditions.

### Pressure plate and cover

**Function.** Clamps and releases the disc.

**Design.** Match flywheel dowels, friction surface, release stroke and clamp load.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Locate cover and tighten progressively to the approved sequence.

**Verify.** Verify even lift or specified release travel and pedal operation.

### Pilot bearing

**Function.** Centers the transmission input relative to the crank where fitted.

**Design.** Match shaft nose, bore and fit.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the specified bearing to the documented depth.

**Verify.** Check fit, rotation and alignment.

### Release bearing

**Function.** Transfers axial force from actuator to spinning clutch.

**Design.** Match release geometry, preload and stroke.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the correct bearing and lubricate only specified surfaces.

**Verify.** Confirm travel without overextension and check for noise.

### Clutch master cylinder

**Function.** Converts pedal travel to hydraulic displacement.

**Design.** Match bore, pedal ratio, stroke and fluid.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit to aligned pedal box and connect approved line.

**Verify.** Measure pedal/release travel and inspect for leakage.

### Clutch slave cylinder

**Function.** Converts hydraulic pressure to clutch release motion.

**Design.** Match concentric or external layout and available stroke.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched actuator and bleed using the maker's method.

**Verify.** Verify clean disengagement without bottoming.

### Shift lever and cables

**Function.** Transmit driver selection to gearbox.

**Design.** Choose cable length, bend radius, lever ratio and detent pattern.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Secure cable housings then adjust end positions using donor references.

**Verify.** Confirm neutral, every gate, reverse lockout and full engagement.

### Input shaft

**Function.** Receives engine torque into the gearbox.

**Design.** Match spline, pilot, bearing fits and torque duty.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit manufactured shaft with correct bearings and retainers during documented rebuild.

**Verify.** Measure endplay, runout and spline condition.

**Function.** Matches rotating speeds before dog engagement.

**Design.** Match cone taper, friction surface and gear clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Inspect matched cone and install ring in its correct orientation.

**Verify.** Measure specified blocking clearance and check synchronization.

### Synchronizer sleeve and hub

**Function.** Lock the selected gear to its shaft.

**Design.** Match spline, dogs, keys, springs and orientation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Assemble in documented order in a clean fixture.

**Verify.** Check movement, detents and complete dog overlap.

### Shift fork and rail

**Function.** Move a sleeve to engage a ratio.

**Design.** Match fork thickness, rail travel and interlock geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit pins and detents correctly and verify single-ratio interlock.

**Verify.** Check fork clearance and every selected position on the bench.

### Gearcase and breather

**Function.** Support shafts, retain lubricant and equalize pressure.

**Design.** Set bearing datums, oil level, vent routing and mount pattern.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use inspected housings with matched dowels, sealant and breathers.

**Verify.** Measure play and inspect vent, seals and leakage.

### Flexplate

**Function.** Couples crank to converter while allowing locating compliance.

**Design.** Match crank balance, converter bolt circle, spacing and starter ring.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the matched plate and correctly seated converter per service data.

**Verify.** Measure flexplate runout and converter mounting clearance.

### Torque converter

**Function.** Transfers launch torque through fluid and may lock mechanically.

**Design.** Match stall behavior, transmission pump drive, pilot and controller.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a rated sealed converter fully seated by the prescribed checks.

**Verify.** Verify seating before mating and commanded slip after commissioning.

**Function.** Provides one central gear member.

**Design.** Match tooth counts, splines and planet set.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

references.title: Build and compare two shifter lever geometries
references.body:
**Objective.** Demonstrate why a short-throw shifter changes effort and travel using an unpowered hand fixture. Materials are a rigid board, hand lever, low-friction retained pivot, two rounded link points, string or guarded teaching link, a ruler, a spring scale and a low-force elastic return. Secure the fixture, protect pinch points and stay within the fixture and scale ratings.

1. Draw one pivot with link attachment radii of 25 and 40 mm, and a hand point 150 mm from the pivot. At small angles, for forces perpendicular to the lever, link travel/hand travel is approximately link radius/hand radius. At a fixed 30 mm hand movement the predictions are about 5 and 8 mm of link travel.
2. Make a card layout. Drill the approved lever material on a clamped backer, deburr holes, assemble with spacers and a retained pivot and fit a low-force load. Confirm collision-free movement and protect fingers.
3. Mark zero without spring slack. At each link radius measure hand travel needed for 5 mm link movement and scale force at matched link load and perpendicular geometry. Ideal predictions are about 30 and 18.75 mm of hand travel. If the link load is 6 N, ideal hand forces are 1.0 and 1.6 N respectively. Friction and changing angles explain some differences.
4. Repeat three trials per configuration. Record units, scatter, pivot play and return-to-neutral behavior. Use a physical stop representing the gearbox's required full engagement. Demonstrate that the shorter option reaches that stop while retaining adequate hand clearance.
5. For a real installation source rated hardware, keep full engagement and reverse/start interlocks, verify cable routing and consult the actual gearbox. The bench lever supplies geometry evidence for a prototype.

**Fresh assignment.** For an 8 mm required link travel and 150 mm hand radius, propose a geometry giving roughly 32 mm of hand movement, build it, measure three repeats and explain the difference from the ideal. The target radius is about 37.5 mm in the small-angle model; the measured result determines acceptance.

writing.title: Design a two-ratio teaching drive
writing.prompt: Select gear pairs for two reductions on your trainer. Draw shafts, supports, guards and the indicator location. Predict turns and direction for each pair. Give the acceptance check and explain which automatic or manual service tasks need vehicle-specific data. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Launch element; Flywheel, flexplate and release; Ratio selection; Shift actuation; Continuously variable drive; Gearbox position and driven axles; Axle differential; Half shafts and propeller shafts. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Predict the gearing change before ordering a differential
writing.prompt: Build a hand-driven shifter or ratio fixture. Record input/output travel or turns, trace detents/retention and compare two setups before selecting donor parts. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.

labs.title: Assemble and measure a gear train
labs.intro: A working hand-driven transmission trainer and its verified ratio sheet. Plan shop time with your supervisor over the sessions the work actually takes.
safety: Use a hand-driven guarded trainer only. Isolate it before adjustment. Keep fingers and loose clothing away from mesh and never energize an open gearbox.
materials: Hand-driven teaching gears and supported shafts
steps: Assemble a selected pair and mark shaft zeros.
Count input and output turns over several complete cycles. Reverse by hand to identify lost motion.
Isolate one gear as instructed and measure backlash at the specified point. Reassemble a second ratio or inspect a second gear pair.
Compare actual and predicted results, then identify one measurement that would differ on a limited-slip or automatic system.

questions.prompt: What did you personally make or service? Record actual conditions, measured values, instruments, and any specialist operations.

Both tooth-count and shaft-mark methods support the reported ratio, with repeatable lash readings. Record your result, corrections, retest and sign-off status. Include the witness name and date where required.
Which rule, authority or shop control applied at this site? Identify the actor, triggering operation, source and the record kept.

Name the actual part or trainer component and the design alternative you considered. Record the observed or measured result, units and conditions where applicable, and its effect on the as-built decision.
Identify one fitted part and each fastener, seal, clip or connector that you personally handled. Record parent assembly, position, source, required and observed quantity, and evidence.

labs.photos: Attach dated photographs of your own work, with part or revision identification. An instructor may also document direct observation.
